claims: "Self-Adjusting Tensions System" that is "fully automatic" (manufacturer claim, product page; the manual shows an Auto Tension Dial set per stitch)
"Heavy Duty Metal Frame" (manufacturer claim; the page says only the interior frame is metal)
"High Speed Stitching" and "Professional speed" at 1,300/min (manufacturer claim, product page)
"Powerful motor" for denim and canvas (manufacturer FAQ claim; motor type and output are not published)

conflicts: Weight: the Singer product page shows 18.6 with no unit, while the Singer manual gives 9.0 kg (19.84 lb); the manual figure is used.

Dimensions: the Singer product page shows 13.5 x 10.5 x 11.5 with no unit or axis labels, while the manual gives 360 x 290 x 300 mm (about 14.2 x 11.4 x 11.8 in, W x D x H); our earlier spec held only a width of 11.5, and the manual figures are used.

Tension: Singer's page calls it a 'self-adjusting' system, while the manual shows an Auto Tension Dial set per stitch and says to adjust in small steps if results differ; we treat the page wording as a maker claim.

Warranty: the 25 year, 2 year and 90 day terms come from Singer's generic warranty document, not a model-specific one, and Singer reserves the right to reject claims on machines from unauthorized dealers, including unauthorized internet sites.

Price: Sewing Machines Plus via Walmart showed $626.18 on 2026-09-29, Best Buy $649.99 and GoldStar Tool $699.00 in earlier checks, and the Singer store showed $649.99 against an MSRP of $819.99 on 2026-10-02; dealers set their own price.
Type: sold as a serger; it is a serger and coverstitch combination that needs a manual conversion, recorded as 'serger' with the combination noted.

ownerThemes.theme: Owners like getting a 5-thread serger and coverstitch in one box for roughly $450 to $650 and report clean stitches once set up.
In coverstitch mode there is little room under the foot; pressing the lifter bar further down helps slide fabric in. Some report the right needle skipping and the triple cover never forming.
Singer 2022 needles are required and hard to find, especially size 11; threading is described as difficult until learned.

editorial.verdict: A 5-thread serger and coverstitch in one box at 1,300 spm, with a manual changeover each time you switch and many owner threads about threading trouble.
editorial.whoFor: A sewist short on space or budget who wants a 5-thread safety stitch and coverstitch in one machine and accepts a changeover between modes.
editorial.skipIf: You switch between seaming and hemming often in one project, or want a stated free arm or thread trimmer; Singer publishes neither.
editorial.keySpec: 2/3/4/5 thread · serger + coverstitch · 1,300 spm · 3.0 to 9.8 mm width · 19.84 lb
strengths: Singer lists 14 stitches with 2 to 5 thread capability and a coverstitch in one machine, which the 14HD854 and 14CG754 pages do not offer.
Singer's manual publishes the working ranges: differential feed 1:0.6 to 1:2.0, overedge width 3.0 to 9.8 mm, stitch length 1 to 4 mm, presser foot rise 4.5 mm.
Owners report pleasing cover stitch and general stitch results in some threads, and Sewing Machines Plus shows 4.78 from 9 reviews (a small sample).
weaknesses: Owners report threading and looper trouble across 21 statements, including looper threads that never interlock and painful frequent switching between serger and coverstitch.
Owners report defects and skipped stitches in 15 statements, mostly from help-seeking Reddit threads, so this is not a failure rate.
Owners report the auto tension dial still needs adjusting, and Singer's manual says to adjust in small steps if results differ.

checks.title: Weight and size
checks.body: Singer's page shows 18.6 and 13.5 x 10.5 x 11.5 with no units; the manual gives 9.0 kg (19.84 lb) and 360 x 290 x 300 mm. Use the manual figures when planning bench space.

checks.title: Needles
checks.body: The manual allows only Singer 2022 needles in 14/90 (supplied) and 11/80, and warns against standard household needles. Owners report these are hard to find.

checks.title: Seller and warranty
checks.body: Singer's 25 year, 2 year and 90 day warranty is a generic document and Singer may reject claims from unauthorized dealers. Confirm the seller before buying.

realCost: Serger thread: up to five cones for the 5-thread safety stitch, with cone adapters and thread nets on the accessory list
Singer 2022 needles in 14/90 and 11/80; the manual allows only these
Serger oil and brush; an oiler and brush are on the accessory list
Spare knife: one extra is included per the Singer page

faqs.a: Yes. Singer's page says it comes with coverstitch, and the manual shows a clutch change and cover stitch needles. Cover stitch needle gauges are 2.8 mm and 5.6 mm.

faqs.q: How long does it take to switch from serger to coverstitch?
faqs.a: Singer does not publish a changeover time, so it is [verify]. Owners report switching often is painful.
Singer 2022 (EL x 705), with 14/90 supplied; the manual says use only 14/90 and 11/80.

Singer calls it a self-adjusting tension system. The manual shows an Auto Tension Dial that you set per stitch, based on medium weight fabric and 60 polyester spun thread, with small adjustments if results differ.
The manual gives 9.0 kg, which is 19.84 lb. Singer's page shows 18.6 with no unit, so the sources disagree.
The manual gives 360 x 290 x 300 mm, about 14.2 x 11.4 x 11.8 in (W x D x H). The page shows 13.5 x 10.5 x 11.5 with no unit or axis labels.

faqs.q: Does it have a free arm or thread trimmer?
faqs.a: Singer publishes neither for this model, so both are [verify]. The knife trims the fabric edge only.

Singer's generic document gives 25 years on the frame, 2 years on electrical parts and 90 days on mechanical parts, for household use, to the first purchaser. Singer may reject claims on machines from unauthorized dealers.

Amazon shows 4.2 from 1,501 ratings, pooled with the B0GM81RNCC listing, so it is not for this model alone. Sewing Machines Plus shows 4.78 from 9 reviews, and Singer's own page shows 4.3 from 62 (the page's own figure).
Singer's page says Heavy Duty Metal Frame but states only the interior frame is metal. Heavy duty is a Singer claim, and one owner calls it mostly plastic.
Singer does not publish motor type or output. The page lists 0.5 amps, 114 watts, 120 volts and 60 Hz as electrical input.
